For my entire life my biggest issue is that I am worried about being betrayed or hurt by others.  It seems silly, but I have always had a defense of making sure I am prepared to betray them before they can betray me.  I live with fear and then I add stress to it by never truly being loyal or faithful to anyone from my employer to my friends to my spouse.  I try to keep my life set up so that I can leave them and be with out them at any moment.  I have tried therapy for years, I used to go to yoga, I have tried spiritual activities like Buddhism, yoga, reading, exercising.  But I always live with this fear and anxiety.  I get a little better every day but it has been a process that has been going on for over 20 years of my life.  Is there anything I can do to heal myself?

text: Is this logical, coherent, well-written and scientific paragraph: "In the scientific literature surrounding psychology, judgment and decision-making, the terms “complexity” and “complex decision-making” are frequently used in a broad sense. Hence, it might be useful to begin by providing a clear and concise definition of complexity. According to Bennet and Bennet (2004), complexity refers to the state of a system, situation, or problem where a certain level of order exists, but the excessive number of elements and interconnected parts makes it impossible to understand through simple analytic or logical ways. At its extreme, a complex situation exhibits a landscape rich in extensive connections, diverse relationships, and dynamic interdependencies among various events and processes (Bennett & Bennet, 2008). Although trends and patterns may exist, their entanglement often renders them indiscernible, exacerbated by factors such as time delays, nonlinearity, and a complex web of feedback loops. To put it simply, complexity refers to the state of a system, situation, or problem that make it challenging to understand and discern underlying trends and patterns. " Suggest improvments if needed
required_facts: Paragraph introduces the terms "complexity" and "complex decision-making" in the psychology/judgment and decision-making literature
Cites Bennet and Bennet (2004): complexity is a state where some order exists but too many elements and interconnected parts make it impossible to understand through simple analytic or logical ways
Cites Bennett & Bennet (2008): at its extreme, a complex situation has extensive connections, diverse relationships and dynamic interdependencies among events and processes
Trends and patterns may exist but are hard to discern due to time delays, nonlinearity and feedback loops
